summary: Device token selection after the head: greedy with index tie-break, or temperature / top-k / top-p sampling with Core's seeded counter-based draws
implementation_scope: Two-stage CUDA top-k (256 block slices, then one global block), tempered weights, top-p prefix and one draw per token from Core's counter-based uniform (crit/sampling.h) at a position advanced on the device. The host oracle is Core's Sampler; an FP64 Python mirror uses Core's draw bit for bit. Logit processing before selection and per-request parameter storage are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Logits are produced on the device and requests need temperature, top-k or top-p sampling with reproducible seeds
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Only greedy decoding is served, or selection must include penalties, biases or grammars that are not applied to the logits first
provides: Rank order by logit with lowest-index tie-break; greedy path
Top-k up to 64 candidates over a full vocabulary in two device stages
Temperature weights, top-p rank prefix and one draw per sampled token
Core's Philox draw on the device at a device-advanced position, so device tokens equal crit::core::Sampler's away from FP32 rounding
FP64 Python mirror of the device rules with Core's bit-identical draw
engine_supplies: The logits row on the device and the candidate scratch
Per-sequence Params with the position set to the committed output count
Logit processing (penalties, biases, constraints) before selection
Keeping greedy requests on their existing argmax path where bit identity matters
preserve: One draw per sampled token from Core's uniform at the request's own seed, stream and position
Top-p over the top-k candidates in rank order, keeping at least one
adapt: Fusing selection into the head or capturing it in the decode graph
Additional truncation rules on the same candidate list

code_files.purpose: Params and the selection launch interface
Two-stage top-k selection, tempered top-p draw with Core's uniform and device position advance
FP64 Python mirror of the device rules with Core's Philox draw and a runnable example

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 and Core's sampling header (crit::core) for the device path; Python 3.11+ standard library for the mirror
requires.model: One logits row per selected token
requires.workload: Generation that samples with temperature, top-k or top-p and needs reproducible seeds

contract.input: Device logits row and vocabulary size; device Params; scratch for 256 x 64 candidates
contract.output: The selected token index in device memory; Params.position advanced by one
contract.ownership: The engine owns logits, Params, scratch and output; kernels borrow them on the caller's stream
contract.failure: Null pointers or an empty vocabulary are rejected at launch; NaN logits are not filtered; FP32 weights can pick a neighbouring token when a draw lands within rounding of a boundary
contract.core_boundary: Sampling rules, the draw and the host sampler are Core's (crit/sampling.h: uniform, SamplingParams, resolve_sampling, Sampler); this entry is the device path of steps 7 to 12 with top_k capped at 64. Engines report support through ModelInfo::sampling and read SamplingOptions in Model::open_request

dependencies: Python standard library for the mirror

validation.host: Core's sampling fixture covers the rules, the generator and Sampler; the Python mirror is checked against Core's Philox vectors and Sampler draws, plus greedy ties, nucleus membership and top-k/top-p reductions
validation.native: Greedy ties, top-k 1 and tiny top-p reducing to greedy, position advance and repeatability, every draw inside Core's kept set and equal to crit::core::Sampler::sample away from boundaries, and frequencies within four standard errors of the tempered distribution
